description: Our project is unique; it involves programming a game, but in a way that is different from what was previously common.
summary:
Lunar Lifeline is an interactive survival game and educational web application designed to build awareness about the interconnected life-support and health challenges astronauts face on the Moon, where help from Earth is days away.
Built by our team using React, Vite, CSS, and custom SVGs, the platform supports 5 languages and features five core sections: Cosmic Animation (spacewalk, helmet HUD, Earth, Moon, and Mars visuals), Moon Health (tracking astronaut mood, sleep, heart rate, and anxiety), NASA Research (4 real NASA studies on space physiology), NASA Links (12 official portals including the Open Data Catalog), and Mission Stats (logging wins, losses, and causes of failure). In the 5-minute survival game, players must balance three interdependent resources—oxygen, food, and energy—where generating one depletes another, while rapidly repairing a failing generator before energy drains four times faster.
This project addresses the critical need to understand human survival in isolated lunar habitats. By turning authentic NASA data into high-stakes, decision-driven gameplay, Lunar Lifeline proves that space exploration isn't just about reaching the Moon—it is about ensuring a Safe Return.
details:
Overview & How It Works:
Lunar Lifeline is an interactive, simulation-driven web application and game designed to monitor, measure, and visualize vital human health indicators during simulated lunar missions. Players manage critical astronaut crew metrics—such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, fatigue, and cognitive stress levels—in real time. As mission conditions change, player decisions directly impact these physiological parameters, dynamically altering both crew survival probabilities and the surrounding lunar habitat environment.
Benefits & Intended Impact:
The core benefit of Lunar Lifeline lies in translating complex biomedical telemetry into an intuitive, actionable, and engaging visual experience. In long-duration spaceflight, minor physiological anomalies can quickly escalate into mission-critical emergencies. By simulating these cause-and-effect relationships, Lunar Lifeline serves as both an educational tool for the public and a conceptual training simulator that highlights the importance of proactive health monitoring, preventive care, and rapid crisis management in extreme environments.
Tools, Languages & Technologies Used:
To ensure high performance, cross-platform compatibility, and responsive real-time rendering, the project was engineered using a modern web stack:
• Frontend & Simulation Engine: React, Vite, JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, and CSS3.
• Graphics & Data Visualization: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) for crisp, dynamic rendering of crew vitals, mission telemetry, and interactive UI components.
• Data & Intelligence: NASA Open Science Data and physiological research baselines to model realistic biological responses, paired with intelligent predictive logic to simulate cascading health effects.
• Deployment & Version Control: Git, GitHub, and Vercel for continuous integration and instant global accessibility.
Creativity & Key Considerations:
What sets Lunar Lifeline apart is its gamified approach to space medicine—moving away from static data tables to create a living, reactive ecosystem where human biology dictates gameplay mechanics. Throughout development, we prioritized three core factors:
• Scientific Realism: Grounding vital sign thresholds and environmental stressors in documented spaceflight health data.
• Accessibility: Building a lightweight, browser-based architecture that runs smoothly on standard devices without requiring specialized hardware or installations.
• User Experience (UX): Designing a clean, high-contrast telemetry interface that allows users to interpret complex crew health data at a glance under simulated time pressure.
